data.name: Maqsurah
data.long_meaning: In Islamic culture, Maqsurah is derived from the Arabic root word 'qasara', which means to be short, enclosed, or confined. This name symbolizes protection, safety, and security. It is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-An'am (6:111) where Allah Almighty says, 'And We have already sent a Messenger (Muhammad) to every community (saying): 'Worship Allah alone and avoid Taghoot (all false deities).' Therefore, Maqsurah can be seen as a name that signifies being protected under the care and guidance of Allah.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maqsurah holds deep cultural significance in Islamic society, symbolizing safety, protection, and security. The word is derived from the Arabic root 'qasara', meaning to be short, enclosed, or confined. Thus, this name is believed to signify a state of being sheltered within a specific location. Historically, fortresses, mosques, and even cities were given this name to convey a sense of fortification and security.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Maqsurah carries immense weight in Islamic theology. It is mentioned in the Holy Quran in Surah Al-An'am (6:111), where Allah Almighty commands the followers to worship Him alone and avoid idolatry and false deities. The term 'Maqsurah' here represents the concept of being under the protection and guidance of Allah. It signifies a sacred space, where the worshipper is shielded from worldly distractions and focused on their devotion to Allah. In this sense, it can be seen as a reminder of the importance of seeking refuge in Allah and submitting to His Divine Will.
